payload.task_text:
You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

nodes.text:
You are helping prepare a literature review on transformer architectures in NLP. Nine arXiv papers have already been downloaded into the arxiv_local MCP storage. Your job is to read each one and report back a compact digest.

For EACH of these paper IDs, call mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper with the paper_id and extract the ABSTRACT section only (do not report full paper content):
- 2009.06732 (Efficient Transformers: A Survey)
- 1706.03762 (Attention Is All You Need)
- 1810.04805 (BERT)
- 2005.14165 (Language Models are Few-Shot Learners / GPT-3)
- 1910.10683 (T5 - Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning)
- 1409.0473 (Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate / Bahdanau attention)
- 1207.00580 (Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors / Dropout)
- 1502.03167 (Batch Normalization)
- 1312.06199 (Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning)

Deliverable — for each paper ID return:
1. Title and authors (as found in the paper)
2. The abstract, condensed to 2-3 sentences max (keep the essential claims)
3. One sentence stating what the paper covers / contributes

Also report any paper ID that fails to read. Keep the whole response concise; do not paste full sections.
Read 9 arXiv papers abstracts

Create a Notion database named exactly "Research Paper Tracker" at the workspace root (parent = {"workspace": true}), then create exactly 9 database entry pages in it. Do not create any extra pages or databases.

DATABASE SCHEMA — properties (use these exact names and types):
- "Title": title type
- "Paper_ID": rich_text
- "Authors": rich_text
- "Year": number
- "Category": select with exactly these options: "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey"
- "Source": select with exactly these options: "Scholarly", "Arxiv", "Both"
- "Abstract_Summary": rich_text

PAGE DATA — create one page per entry below (9 pages). Use standard Notion property value formats (title array with text content, rich_text arrays, number, select {"name": ...}):

1. Title: "Efficient Transformers: A Survey" | Paper_ID: "2009.06732" | Authors: "Yi Tay, Mostafa Dehghani, Dara Bahri" | Year: 2020 | Category: "Survey" | Source: "Both" | Abstract_Summary: "Comprehensive survey of efficient transformer architectures, covering methods that reduce the computational and memory complexity of transformers."
2. Title: "Attention Is All You Need" | Paper_ID: "1706.03762" | Authors: "Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar" | Year: 2017 | Category: "Architecture Design" | Source: "Both" | Abstract_Summary: "Proposes the Transformer, a new simple network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely."
3. Title: "BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding" | Paper_ID: "1810.04805" | Authors: "Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee" | Year: 2018 | Category: "Training Methods" | Source: "Both" | Abstract_Summary: "Introduces BERT, a language representation model designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text; the pre-trained model can be fine-tuned for various tasks."
4. Title: "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners" | Paper_ID: "2005.14165" | Authors: "Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder" | Year: 2020 | Category: "Architecture Design" | Source: "Both" | Abstract_Summary: "Presents GPT-3, a large Transformer-based neural language model; scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance."
5. Title: "Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer" | Paper_ID: "1910.10683" | Authors: "Colin Raffel, Noam Shazeer, Adam Roberts" | Year: 2019 | Category: "Training Methods" | Source: "Both" | Abstract_Summary: "Introduces a unified framework (T5) that converts all text-based language problems into a text-to-text format for transfer learning."
6. Title: "Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate" | Paper_ID: "1409.0473" | Authors: "Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio" | Year: 2014 | Category: "Applications" | Source: "Both" | Abstract_Summary: "Proposes an attention mechanism for neural machine translation that lets the network automatically search for parts of a source sentence relevant to predicting a target word."
7. Title: "Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors" | Paper_ID: "1207.00580" | Authors: "Geoffrey E. Hinton, Nitish Srivastava" | Year: 2012 | Category: "Training Methods" | Source: "Arxiv" | Abstract_Summary: "Describes dropout, a technique for addressing overfitting in neural networks."
8. Title: "Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training" | Paper_ID: "1502.03167" | Authors: "Sergey Ioffe, Christian Szegedy" | Year: 2015 | Category: "Training Methods" | Source: "Arxiv" | Abstract_Summary: "Proposes batch normalization to address the shifting distribution of layer inputs during training, accelerating deep network training."
9. Title: "Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning" | Paper_ID: "1312.06199" | Authors: "Volodymyr Mnih, Koray Kavukcuoglu" | Year: 2013 | Category: "Training Methods" | Source: "Arxiv" | Abstract_Summary: "Presents the first deep neural network model to successfully learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory input using reinforcement learning."

PROCEDURE:
1. Call mcp__notion__API-create-a-database with parent {"workspace": true}, title "Research Paper Tracker", and the property schema above (for select types include the options list).
2. Capture the returned database id.
3. For each of the 9 entries, call mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"database_id": "<the db id>"} and the property values.
4. Verify by calling mcp__notion__API-post-database-query on the database and confirming 9 pages exist.

DELIVERABLE (report back): the database id, the created database URL if available, the list of created page IDs with their titles, and the verification query result count. Note any page-creation failures explicitly.
Create Notion paper tracker DB

Create a Microsoft Word document named Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in this directory:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Transformer_Literature_Review.docx

Use the word MCP tools (mcp__word__create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph). Build content in exact order:

1. TITLE: heading (use add_heading, high prominence) with exactly the text:
"Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP"

2. HEADING "Introduction" (Heading level 1), then this introduction paragraph:
"This review surveys the development of transformer architectures in natural language processing (NLP). The corpus was assembled by querying two academic databases: a scholarly catalog searched with the phrases 'transformer' and 'attention mechanism', and the arXiv repository searched with the phrases 'transformer' and 'neural network'. The results of each pair of searches were combined (union) and deduplicated by paper identifier, yielding nine unique papers, six of which appear in both databases. Each paper is classified into one of four methodology categories - Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, and Survey - based on keyword evidence from its title and abstract. Papers appearing in both databases are marked as [Both databases]. The review traces the field from the attention mechanisms that preceded the transformer, through the founding architecture and its pre-training and scaling recipes, to the efficiency surveys that consolidate the state of the art."

3. HEADING "Architecture Design" (Heading level 1), then a paragraph: "Papers proposing new model architectures or structural innovations." Then for each of the two papers below, add a paragraph with the paper entry (bolding the title via the tool's bold option is fine, otherwise leave as plain text), and a second paragraph with its description:

Paper A entry paragraph: "Attention Is All You Need - Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar (2017) [Paper ID: 1706.03762] [Both databases]"
Paper A description: "The founding paper of the transformer family. It proposes a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Self-attention replaced recurrent layers as the dominant building block for sequence modeling in NLP."

Paper B entry paragraph: "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners - Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder (2020) [Paper ID: 2005.14165] [Both databases]"
Paper B description: "Introduces GPT-3, a large Transformer-based neural language model trained on massive amounts of internet text. The paper demonstrates that scaling up the model architecture greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes matching prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches."

4. HEADING "Training Methods" (Heading level 1), paragraph: "Papers about training techniques, optimization, or learning strategies." Then entries (entry paragraph + description paragraph each):

"BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding - Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee (2018) [Paper ID: 1810.04805] [Both databases]"
Description: "Introduces BERT, designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context. The pre-trained model can be fine-tuned for various downstream tasks, establishing the pre-train then fine-tune recipe as a dominant training paradigm."

"Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer - Colin Raffel, Noam Shazeer, Adam Roberts (2019) [Paper ID: 1910.10683] [Both databases]"
Description: "Introduces T5 and a unified framework that converts all text-based language problems into a text-to-text format, systematically exploring transfer learning objectives, datasets, and training strategies for transformers."

"Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors - Geoffrey E. Hinton, Nitish Srivastava (2012) [Paper ID: 1207.00580]"
Description: "Describes dropout, a technique for addressing overfitting in neural networks. Dropout remains a standard regularization component in transformer training pipelines."

"Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training - Sergey Ioffe, Christian Szegedy (2015) [Paper ID: 1502.03167]"
Description: "Proposes batch normalization to stabilize deep network training by addressing the changing distribution of layer inputs during training, foundational background for the normalization choices used in transformer stacks."

"Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning - Volodymyr Mnih, Koray Kavukcuoglu (2013) [Paper ID: 1312.06199]"
Description: "Presents the first deep neural network model to successfully learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory input using reinforcement learning, illustrating deep learning training strategies beyond language."

5. HEADING "Applications" (Heading level 1), paragraph: "Papers applying transformers and attention to specific NLP tasks or domains." Then:

"Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio (2014) [Paper ID: 1409.0473] [Both databases]"
Description: "Applies attention to neural machine translation, proposing a mechanism that allows the network to automatically search for parts of a source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word. This alignment-based attention is the direct precursor of transformer self-attention."

6. HEADING "Survey" (Heading level 1), paragraph: "Papers that review, survey, or comprehensively analyze the field." Then:

"Efficient Transformers: A Survey - Yi Tay, Mostafa Dehghani, Dara Bahri (2020) [Paper ID: 2009.06732] [Both databases]"
Description: "Provides a comprehensive survey of efficient transformer architectures, covering methods that reduce the computational and memory complexity of transformers, and consolidating the rapidly growing design space."

7. HEADING "Conclusion" (Heading level 1), then this paragraph:
"The collected corpus outlines a clear arc: attention mechanisms first emerged as an application-level fix for fixed-length encoding bottlenecks in neural machine translation (Bahdanau et al., 2014), matured into a standalone architecture with the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017), and then became the substrate for large-scale pre-training (BERT, GPT-3) and unified transfer learning (T5). The trend across publication years, from 2012 to 2020, shows a steady shift from general training techniques such as dropout and batch normalization toward transformer-specific pre-training and scaling strategies. Notable research gaps remain: computational and memory efficiency is still an active frontier despite the breadth of work surveyed by Tay et al. (2020); few papers in the corpus evaluate transformers on standardized benchmarks; summarization, classification, and generation applications are underrepresented in this sample; and questions of interpretability, robustness, and training efficiency of very large models remain open directions for future work."

Requirements: use real heading styles for all headings (not merely bold paragraphs); document must exist and be a valid .docx. After building, read the document back (mcp__word__get_document_text) to verify title, all 7 headings/sections, and all 9 papers appear. Report the final word count of the body text and confirm the file path.
Build Word literature review

Create an Excel workbook at this exact path:
